source: NCERT Class X, Contemporary India II, Geography Ch. 6.

sections.heading: 1. Importance of Manufacturing
points: **Manufacturing** = production of goods in large quantities from raw materials.
It is the **backbone of development** — modernises agriculture, reduces dependence on farming, provides jobs, brings in foreign exchange (exports), and reduces regional disparities.
The share of manufacturing in GDP has stagnated around 17%; the **National Manufacturing Competitiveness Council (NMCC)** aims to raise it and to boost productivity.

sections.heading: 2. Factors of Industrial Location
points: Ideal location = where **raw materials, labour, capital, power and market** are available cheaply.
**Agglomeration economies** — industries cluster in cities to share benefits (e.g. Mumbai, Kolkata, Ahmedabad).
Government policy and specialised labour also influence location.
Industry and agriculture move together — **agro-based** industries use farm produce; industries supply inputs (fertilisers, machines) to farms.

sub: **Agro-based** (cotton, jute, silk, sugar) and **mineral-based** (iron & steel, cement, aluminium).
**Basic/key** (supply raw materials to others, e.g. iron & steel) and **consumer** (goods for direct use, e.g. sugar, toothpaste).

sections.heading: 4. Key Industries
points: **Textile** — cotton textile is the largest industry; first mill at **Mumbai (1854)**; concentrated in Maharashtra/Gujarat; jute mills mostly in the **Hugli basin (West Bengal)**.

**Iron and Steel** — a basic industry; TISCO (Jamshedpur), Bhilai, Rourkela, Durgapur, Bokaro, Vishakhapatnam, Salem; India is a leading crude steel producer; Chotanagpur plateau has most plants (raw materials nearby).
**Aluminium smelting** (NALCO, BALCO); **cement** (needs limestone, coal, gypsum); **automobile, chemical, fertiliser, IT and electronics** (Bengaluru = 'electronic capital').

sections.heading: 5. Industrial Pollution and Control
points: Industries cause **air, water, land, thermal and noise pollution**.
Control measures: **treating effluents, recycling water, rainwater harvesting, reducing smoke (scrubbers), NTPC** (thermal power) as a model of eco-friendly practices.
The **NTPC** adopts pollution control and afforestation as a corporate practice.

sections.heading: 6. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: First cotton textile mill = Mumbai (1854); jute industry = Hugli basin (West Bengal).
Iron & steel = basic industry; TISCO at Jamshedpur (1907); most plants on Chotanagpur plateau.
Agglomeration economies = benefits of industries clustering together.
Bengaluru = electronic/IT capital of India.
NMCC aims to raise manufacturing's share of GDP.

sections.heading: 7. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: The **first cotton mill** was set up in **Mumbai (1854)**.
**Iron and steel** is a **basic/key industry** (supplies others).
The **jute industry** is concentrated in the **Hugli basin (West Bengal)**.
**Cement** needs **limestone, coal and gypsum** as raw materials.
